lines.trans: Hi, Max.
Hi.
I want to move to your place.
Do you have nowhere to live?
No, I have a million options.
Kostya is calling me back.
Leva is also inviting me to live.
But I am ready to live with you.
What do you want to say?
I want to live with you.
I do not want to be without you.
That is very pleasant to hear.

lines.trans: Really?

words.gram: feminine singular, nominative; used as a side word

lines.trans: Yes, I believe you.

meanings.note: Expressive conversational Russian interjection or greeting ('hi') used directly in spoken exchanges.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

переехать.gloss: to move (to a new home or city)

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'ехать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to move', forming an aspectual pair with 'переезжать'.

examples.trans: They moved into a new flat.

examples.text: Ты в Москву переехала, да? Поедем сейчас в сауну, посидим!
examples.trans: You moved to Moscow, right? Let's go to a sauna now and sit for a while!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'to' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.en: there is nowhere (to), no place available
meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'nowhere'.

examples.trans: I have nowhere to spend this night.

examples.text: Да, мне совсем негде жить в Москве.
examples.trans: Yes, I have nowhere to live in Moscow at all.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to live'.

examples.trans: I live in a communal flat.

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
Secondary conversational sense ('there isn't') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: after numbers: два миллиона, пять миллионов

examples.text: Значит, предложение такое. Ты мне говоришь, где твои сорок миллионов.
examples.trans: So, here's the offer. You tell me where your forty million is.

meanings.note: других вариантов нет = there are no other options

examples.text: Пробуем, других вариантов у нас нет.
examples.trans: Let's try it, we have no other options.

examples.text: Это самый лучший вариант для всех.
examples.trans: This is the very best option for everyone.

examples.text: Трава, говорите? Отлично! Пробуем, других вариантов у нас нет.
examples.trans: Herbs, you say? Excellent! Let's try it, we have no other options.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to call', forming an aspectual pair with 'позвать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
как тебя зовут? = what's your name? меня зовут ... = my name is ...
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'ago'.
Secondary conversational sense ('back, backwards') (шаг назад = a step back) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago!

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил! Я сам приказ подписывал!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago! I signed the order myself!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'too'.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'глашать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to invite', forming an aspectual pair with 'пригласить'.

examples.text: Это правильно. Я приглашаю вас в общественный совет.
examples.trans: That's right. I'm inviting you onto the public council.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: usually the short form: я готов (m), я готова (f)
+ instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Secondary conversational sense ('tell me / tell us') (polite request) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'without' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: очень приятно = pleased to meet you

examples.text: Очень приятно. А в чём дело?
examples.trans: Pleased to meet you. So what's the matter?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лышать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to hear', forming an aspectual pair with 'услышать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to hear about') (слышать о + prepositional) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Как странно, я ничего об этом не слышал.
examples.trans: How strange, I've heard nothing about it.

meanings.note: as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to believe', forming an aspectual pair with 'поверить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to believe in') (верить в + accusative) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Go on, tell her. Nina doesn't believe it.
